/-!
# Conjecture 5.26

by H. Koch

Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group with the minimal number of generators $d$, and let $r_1$
(respectively, $r_2$) be the minimal number of defining relations on $d$ generators in the
sense of representing $G$ as a factor-group of a free discrete group (pro-$p$-group). It is
well known that always $r_2 > d^2/4$. For each prime number $p$ denote by $c(p)$ the exact
upper bound for the numbers $b(p)$ with the property that $r_2 \geq b(p) d^2$ for all finite
$p$-groups.

a) It is obvious that $r_1 \geq r_2$. Find a $p$-group with $r_1 > r_2$.

b) *Conjecture:* $\lim_{p \to \infty} c(p) = 1/4$. It is proved (J. Wisliceny,
*Math. Nachr.* **102** (1981), 57–78) that $\lim_{d \to \infty} r_2 / d^2 = 1/4$.

## Formalisation notes

* $d = d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`, the minimal size of a generating set of $G$.
* $r_1(G)$ is `discreteRelationRank G`: the least number of relators in a presentation of $G$
  as a factor-group of the free (discrete) group on $d(G)$ generators.
* $r_2(G)$ is `proPRelationRank p G`. Free pro-$p$ groups are not available in Mathlib, so we
  use the standard identity $r_2(G) = \dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ for the number
  of relations of a minimal pro-$p$ presentation of a finite $p$-group $G$ (see J.-P. Serre,
  *Galois Cohomology*, Chapter I, §4.3, or H. Koch, *Galois Theory of $p$-Extensions*).
  Since $G$ is finite, its continuous cohomology is its cohomology as an abstract group.
* $c(p)$ is `c p`, the supremum of the real numbers $b$ with $r_2(G) \geq b \, d(G)^2$ for
  every finite $p$-group $G$. The limit in part b) is taken along the primes.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- J. Wisliceny, *Zur Darstellung von Pro-p-Gruppen und Lieschen Algebren durch Erzeugende und
  Relationen*, Math. Nachr. **102** (1981), 57–78.
-/

blocks.docstring:
$r_1(G)$: the minimal number of defining relations of a finitely generated group $G$ on
$d = d(G)$ generators, where $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$ (`Group.rank G`).
That is, the least $n$ such that $G \cong F_d / \langle\langle S \rangle\rangle$ for a set $S$ of
$n$ elements of the free (discrete) group $F_d$ on $d$ generators.

When $G$ is finite such a finite presentation always exists, so the infimum is attained.

justification.closest_existing_considered: PresentedGroup, Group.rank, Subgroup.normalClosure (used as building blocks); no Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib notion of relation rank / deficiency exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.26».discreteRelationRank
justification.why_needed: r₁(G): the minimal number of relators in a presentation of G on d(G) = Group.rank G generators as a quotient of the free discrete group. Mathlib has FreeGroup, PresentedGroup and Group.rank but no 'relation rank' / minimal number of relators.

blocks.name: discreteRelationRank
blocks.text:
/--
$r_1(G)$: the minimal number of defining relations of a finitely generated group $G$ on
$d = d(G)$ generators, where $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$ (`Group.rank G`).
That is, the least $n$ such that $G \cong F_d / \langle\langle S \rangle\rangle$ for a set $S$ of
$n$ elements of the free (discrete) group $F_d$ on $d$ generators.

When $G$ is finite such a finite presentation always exists, so the infimum is attained.
-/
noncomputable def discreteRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G))),
    S.card = n ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (S : Set (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G)))) ≃* G)}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def proPRelationRank (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank (ZMod p) (groupCohomology.H2 (Rep.trivial (ZMod p) G (ZMod p)))
blocks.docstring:
$r_2(G)$: the minimal number of defining relations of a finite $p$-group $G$ on $d(G)$
generators, in the sense of representing $G$ as a factor-group of the free pro-$p$ group on
$d(G)$ generators. This equals $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ (cohomology with
coefficients in the trivial module $\mathbb{F}_p$), which is how it is defined here.

justification.closest_existing_considered: groupCohomology.H2 / Rep.trivial (used); searched Mathlib for pro-p, profinite completion, free pro-p group — none exist.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.26».proPRelationRank
justification.why_needed: r₂(G): the minimal number of relations of G as a quotient of the free pro-p group on d(G) generators. Mathlib has no free pro-p groups or pro-p completions, so it is defined by the standard equivalent characterization Module.finrank (ZMod p) (groupCohomology.H2 (Rep.trivial (ZMod p) G (ZMod p))) (Serre, Galois Cohomology I.4.3; Koch, Galois Theory of p-Extensions).

blocks.name: proPRelationRank
blocks.text:
/--
$r_2(G)$: the minimal number of defining relations of a finite $p$-group $G$ on $d(G)$
generators, in the sense of representing $G$ as a factor-group of the free pro-$p$ group on
$d(G)$ generators. This equals $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ (cohomology with
coefficients in the trivial module $\mathbb{F}_p$), which is how it is defined here.
-/
noncomputable def proPRelationRank (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank (ZMod p) (groupCohomology.H2 (Rep.trivial (ZMod p) G (ZMod p)))

blocks.docstring:
$c(p)$: the exact upper bound (supremum) of the numbers $b$ such that $r_2(G) \geq b \, d(G)^2$
for all finite $p$-groups $G$.

The trivial group has $d = 0$ and $r_2 = 0$, so it imposes no constraint on $b$. For a prime
$p$ the set of such $b$ contains $0$ and is bounded above by $1$ (take $G$ cyclic of order
$p$), so the supremum is a genuine one.

justification.closest_existing_considered: sSup over ℝ (Real.sSup) directly; no existing definition of this constant.
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.26».c
justification.why_needed: The constant c(p) of the problem: sSup of the set of real b with r₂(G) ≥ b·d(G)² for all finite p-groups G. Problem-specific.

blocks.name: c
blocks.text:
/--
$c(p)$: the exact upper bound (supremum) of the numbers $b$ such that $r_2(G) \geq b \, d(G)^2$
for all finite $p$-groups $G$.

The trivial group has $d = 0$ and $r_2 = 0$, so it imposes no constraint on $b$. For a prime
$p$ the set of such $b$ contains $0$ and is bounded above by $1$ (take $G$ cyclic of order
$p$), so the supremum is a genuine one.
-/
noncomputable def c (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {b : ℝ | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], IsPGroup p G →
    b * (Group.rank G : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ proPRelationRank p G}

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem discreteRelationRank_le {G : Type*} [Group G] [Group.FG G]
    (S : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G))))
    (e : PresentedGroup (S : Set (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G)))) ≃* G) :
    discreteRelationRank G ≤ S.card :=
  Nat.sInf_le ⟨S, rfl, ⟨e⟩⟩
blocks.docstring:
If $G \cong F_{d(G)} / \langle\langle S \rangle\rangle$ for a finite set $S$ of relators, then
$r_1(G) \leq |S|$.
blocks.name: discreteRelationRank_le
blocks.text:
/--
If $G \cong F_{d(G)} / \langle\langle S \rangle\rangle$ for a finite set $S$ of relators, then
$r_1(G) \leq |S|$.
-/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem discreteRelationRank_le {G : Type*} [Group G] [Group.FG G]
    (S : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G))))
    (e : PresentedGroup (S : Set (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G)))) ≃* G) :
    discreteRelationRank G ≤ S.card :=
  Nat.sInf_le ⟨S, rfl, ⟨e⟩⟩

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem proPRelationRank_of_subsingleton (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G]
    [Subsingleton G] : proPRelationRank p G = 0 := by
  have := ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton.1
    (isZero_groupCohomology_succ_of_subsingleton (Rep.trivial (ZMod p) G (ZMod p)) 1)
  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem c_nonneg (p : ℕ) : 0 ≤ c p := by
  by_cases h : BddAbove {b : ℝ | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], IsPGroup p G →
      b * (Group.rank G : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ proPRelationRank p G}
  · exact le_csSup h fun G _ _ _ => by simp
  · rw [c, Real.sSup_of_not_bddAbove h]

claims.decomposer_note: A 'find an example' problem, formalized (as the repo does for such problems) as the existence Prop: ∃ prime p and finite p-group G with r₁(G) > r₂(G), where d = d(G) is the minimal number of generators, r₁(G) = min number of relators over all presentations of G on d generators as a quotient of the free discrete group F_d (min number of normal generators of the kernel of a surjection F_d → G), and r₂(G) the analogue for the free pro-p group on d generators (equivalently dim_{F_p} H²(G, F_p)); the sentence 'It is obvious that r₁ ≥ r₂' is background, not a question, and the problem is still open (no \zva star).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same existence Prop (∃ prime p, finite p-group G, r₂(G) < r₁(G)) with ∧ rather than →, and agree on the modeling: d = minimal number of generators, r₁ = min number of relators over all presentations of G as a quotient of the free discrete group on d generators, r₂ = dim_{F_p} H²(G, F_p) (standard identity for the relation rank of a minimal pro-p presentation; Mathlib has no free pro-p groups; also the sense in which the quoted Golod–Shafarevich bound r₂ > d²/4 is stated). c07 was chosen as the base because it uses Mathlib's Group.rank (rather than a bespoke generatorRank as in c02/c04/c05), Mathlib's groupCohomology (rather than c04's hand-rolled cochains), the literal PresentedGroup S ≃* G reading of 'factor-group of a free discrete group', natural argument order (c03 puts G first), and no unnecessary `if p.Prime` guard (c06). For finite G the sInf set is nonempty (Schreier), so no junk value is reachable. The declaration is used verbatim; API/test lemmas were composed from c07 (c_nonneg), c03/c07 (discreteRelationRank_le) and c01 (proPRelationRank_of_subsingleton).

claims.decomposer_note: Prop: Tendsto c atTop (nhds (1/4)) along primes p (Filter.atTop restricted to Nat.Prime), where c(p) := sSup {b : ℝ | ∀ finite p-group G, r₂(G) ≥ b · d(G)²} (equivalently inf over nontrivial finite p-groups of r₂(G)/d(G)²; the trivial group has d = 0 and imposes no constraint, and the quoted known bound r₂ > d²/4 gives c(p) ≥ 1/4, so the conjecture is really c(p) → 1/4 from above); the surrounding remarks 'It is well known that r₂ > d²/4' and Wisliceny's theorem lim_{d→∞} r₂/d² = 1/4 are cited known facts framing the conjecture, not questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: Tendsto c (atTop ⊓ 𝓟 {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) (𝓝 (1/4 : ℝ)) with c p := sSup {b : ℝ | ∀ finite p-group G, b·d(G)² ≤ r₂(G)}, exactly the notebook's 'exact upper bound for the numbers b with r₂ ≥ b d² for all finite p-groups' and a limit along primes (repo idiom, cf. GreensOpenProblems/27). Boundary cases checked: trivial group has d = 0 and r₂ = 0, so it imposes no constraint; for prime p the set contains 0 and is bounded above by 1 (cyclic group of order p has d = 1, r₂ = 1), so Real.sSup is the genuine supremum; c at non-primes is filtered out. c02/c04/c05's Nat.Primes/comap version is equivalent but less idiomatic here; c06's if-guard is unnecessary. Elaboration verified: 1/4 is real, filter is on ℕ.

* $d = d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`, the minimal size of a generating set of $G$.
* $r_1(G)$ is `discreteRelationRank G`: the least number of relators in a presentation of $G$

- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

$d = d(G)$ generators, where $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$ (`Group.rank G`).
That is, the least $n$ such that $G \cong F_d / \langle\langle S \rangle\rangle$ for a set $S$ of
$n$ elements of the free (discrete) group $F_d$ on $d$ generators.

When $G$ is finite such a finite presentation always exists, so the infimum is attained.
-/
noncomputable def discreteRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G))),
    S.card = n ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (S : Set (FreeGroup (Fin (Group.rank G)))) ≃* G)}

/--
$r_2(G)$: the minimal number of defining relations of a finite $p$-group $G$ on $d(G)$
generators, in the sense of representing $G$ as a factor-group of the free pro-$p$ group on
$d(G)$ generators. This equals $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ (cohomology with
coefficients in the trivial module $\mathbb{F}_p$), which is how it is defined here.

/--
$c(p)$: the exact upper bound (supremum) of the numbers $b$ such that $r_2(G) \geq b \, d(G)^2$

items: r₂ is defined as dim_{F_p} H²(G, F_p) (Mathlib's abstract group cohomology of the finite group G with trivial coefficients ZMod p) rather than via the free pro-p group, which Mathlib lacks. This equality is a standard theorem for finitely generated pro-p groups (Serre, Galois Cohomology I §4.3; Koch; NSW 3.9.5), and for finite G continuous and abstract cohomology agree. The decomposition notes explicitly sanction this equivalent form.

r₁ takes the minimum over all presentations on exactly d = Group.rank G generators (all surjections F_d → G), counting relators as a Finset. discreteRelationRank assumes only Group.FG (needed for Group.rank); for a non-finitely-presented FG group the sInf would be of an empty set (= 0), but the statements only apply it to finite groups, where a finite presentation on d generators always exists.

Finite p-group is modeled as (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] with IsPGroup p G and p.Prime (p.Prime asserted in part a; in part b the limit filter is restricted to primes, so c p at non-primes is irrelevant). G is quantified over Type (universe 0) because Rep k G requires k and G in the same universe.

c p is sSup over ℝ; the defining set contains 0 and is bounded above by 1 (cyclic group of order p), so no Real.sSup default-value issue arises; the trivial group (d = 0) is harmless. The known bound r₂ > d²/4 is background and not formalized.
The limit p → ∞ over primes is expressed with the repo idiom Tendsto c (atTop ⊓ 𝓟 {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) (𝓝 (1/4)).
Part a ('Find a p-group with r₁ > r₂') is stated as a plain existence theorem (not answer(sorry) ↔ …), following the decomposition table; the remark 'It is obvious that r₁ ≥ r₂' is not formalized.
An extra proven API lemma c_nonneg (0 ≤ c p) is included as a basic sanity test of the bespoke definition c, per the repo's request to add basic API for bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compiled and converged on the same modeling, and none objected to the decomposition. The main (accepted) modeling choice is r₂(G) := dim_{F_p} H²(G, F_p) in place of the literal 'minimal number of relations as a quotient of the free pro-p group on d generators'; this is a standard theorem (Serre, Galois Cohomology I §4.3; Koch) and is explicitly sanctioned by the decomposition notes, and it is the form in which the notebook's own quoted bound r₂ > d²/4 (Golod–Shafarevich) is stated. r₁ is read as the minimum over ALL d(G)-generator discrete presentations (the natural reading of 'minimal number of defining relations on d generators'). Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), forced by Rep k G needing k and G in one universe; harmless since every finite group has a copy there and the invariants are isomorphism-invariant. Part (a) is a 'find an example' problem stated as an existence Prop per the table (no answer(sorry)); part (b) is a conjecture, stated as a plain Prop. Background remarks (r₁ ≥ r₂ obvious, r₂ > d²/4, Wisliceny's theorem) are only recorded in the docstring. Final file compiles with only the two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Three short fully-proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions are included per CONTRIBUTING.md.
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $p\hskip0.2ex $-group with the minimal number of generators $d$, and let $r_1$ (respectively, $r_2$) be the minimal number of defining relations on $d$ generators in the sense of representing $G$ as a factor-group of a free discrete group (pro-$p\hskip0.2ex $-group). It is well known that always $r_2 > d^2/4$. For each prime number $p$ denote by $c(p)$ the exact upper bound for the numbers $b(p)$ with the property that $r_2 \geq b(p)d^2$ for all finite $p\hskip0.2ex $-groups.

a) It is obvious that $r_1 \geq r_2$. Find a $p\hskip0.2ex $-group with $r_1 > r_2$.

b) Conjecture: $\lim\limits_{p\rightarrow
\infty}
c(p)=1/4$. It is proved (J. Wisliceny, Math. Nachr., 102 (1981), 57–78) that $\lim\limits_{d\rightarrow \infty} r_2\left/ d^2\right. =1/4$.
